newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: PRESS DIGEST-Australian General News - July 18.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST-Australian General News - July 18.

text.p: (Compiled for Reuters by Media Monitors)
THE AUSTRALIAN FINANCIAL REVIEW

Reserve Bank of Australia governor Ian Macfarlane said in a strongly worded statement yesterday that he was satisfied WMC Ltd managing director Hugh Morgan had fulfilled his obligations as a member of the RBA Board, and did not act improperly in relation to the Reserve's recent sale of A$2.4 billion of gold reserves. Page 1.

Prime Minister John Howard has reached the middle of his term of office, and professional pollsters and researchers say the speed to collapse of his personal standing has been the most striking feature of his political decline. Howard has been publicly citicised by corporate figures such as National Australia Bank head Don Argus, Coles Myer's Stan Wallis, and former News Ltd head Ken Cowley. Page 1.

A pay deal between Ford Australia and unions which was finalised last week will see workers enjoying a 15.75 per cent pay rise over the next three years, coupled with significant improvements in areas such as long-service leave, voluntary redundancy payouts, and the use of accumulated sick days. Page 3.

As enterprise bargaining negotiations between Telstra and unions begin today, Telstra group managing director, employee relations, Rob Cartwright, has told staff that while management will offer an across-the-board salary increase, it wishes to see major performance improvements in return, and will look at introducing bonus payments based on performance. Page 4.
THE AUSTRALIAN

Australian Foreign Minister Alexander Downer has cancelled a visit to Cambodian capital Phnom Penh in a warning to second Prime Minister Hun Sen to restore stability after the country's bloody military coup. It is also thought Downer cancelled the trip so as not to show support for the ousting of first Prime Minister Prince Norodom Ranariddh. Page 1.

Following fears for his safety, Greg Domaszewicz, who has been charged with the murder of missing toddler Jaidyn Leskie, has been moved to an isolation cell. Domaszewicz appeared briefly in the Melbourne Magistrates' Court yesterday, where his lawyer, Jon Less, maintained the accused's innocence. Page 1.

In a move that could overhaul the entire coal industry, mining giant Rio Tinto yesterday offered its workers an aggressive enterprise bargaining package that gives workers a pay increase of A$10,000 under the condition that union-dominated practices are scrapped. Page 1.

Federal Education Minister Amanda Vanstone yesterday told the Australian-American Chamber of Commerce in Melbourne that Independent MP Pauline Hanson's policies were built on hate and stemmed from an unhappy childhood. While denying her comments were a personal attack on Hanson, Vanstone then went on to say the media and opponents were using Hanson to discredit Prime Minister John Howard. Page 3.
THE SYDNEY MORNING HERALD

Prime Minister John Howard, the Senate Economic Legislative Committee and the House of Representatives Committee on Financial Institutions will question Reserve Bank of Australia head Ian Macfarlane over the role of WMC Ltd chief Hugh Morgan in the RBA's decision to sell of Australia's gold reserves. Page 1.

Figures compiled by the Higher Education Council show women are moving away from traditional university courses such as teaching and nursing, and are moving to courses such as law and business that have in the past been dominated by males. The figures showed an increase of 10 per cent in law enrolments, and 12 per cent in business enrolments. Page 1.

Private wildlife reserve operator Dr John Walmsley will meet with Olympic officials this afternoon to discuss his proposal to turn a giant derelict brickpit on the Games site at Homebush into a display home for platypuses, echidnas, and kookaburras, the tree animals chosen as mascots for the Games. Page 3.

A Nine Network cameraman was yesterday attacked by a youth wielding a fence paling as he filmed a report about the Villawood housing estate in Sydney's western suburbs. The attack, being investigated by police, comes as the New South Wales Government announced plans to demolish and rebuild the estate. Page 3.
THE AGE

Reserve Bank of Australia governor Ian Macfarlane yesterday defended WMC managing director Hugh Morgan following concerns over Morgan's involvement in the RBA's decision to sell off its gold reserves. Macfarlane also defended the appointment of business people to the Bank's board, saying "potential conflicts" were inevitable. Page 1.

New evidence presented to the Victorian State coroner by the Kew Cottages Parents Association and the Office of the Public Advocate says a map showing fire detectors in a section of the Kew Cottages destroyed in a fire that claimed the lives of nine intelectually disabled men has been fabricated after the event. Page 1.

Prime Minister John Howard will visit 18 electorates in six weeks in an effort to boost polls as he faces the middle of his term of office. Polls released this week showed a narrowing of the margin between the Government and the Labor Party, and Howard will use the parliamentary breaks to visit areas outside the Canberra-Sydney-Melbourne triangle. Page 1.

The annual conference of the Victorian Farmers Federation was held in Collins Place this week, and showed a change in the way farmers are working: all 250 conference delegates turned up in suits and recent research by the Federation showed about 60 per cet of Victoria's 30,000 full-time farmers have a personal computer which they are using to improve farming practices. Page 1.
-- Reuters Sydney Newsroom 61-2 9373-1800
